title: Abyssal Claims: source code of an integration platform for ocean and land environmental data
description:
Source code of Abyssal Claims. Abyssal Claims is an independently developed, non-commercial web platform that brings more than fifty publicly funded environmental datasets together on one interactive three-dimensional map. It began with deep-sea mining and has grown into a working space for ocean and land data, from individual measurements and biodiversity records to seabed contracts and the land-side impacts of mining. Its purpose is to let researchers and other stakeholders explore how these datasets relate: a measurement beside the gridded field it informs, a concession beside the species recorded inside it, and the places where the ocean has hardly been observed at all.

Repository: github.com/ice13ball/something-rare-engine
Platform: something-rare.com
Methods documentation: 10.5281/zenodo.19745884

New in v1.2.0.

  • New layers: Plankton Occurrences, GLODAP Measurements, SOCAT Measurements, WOD Casts, Argo Oxygen Measurements, CoastDOM and Greenland Sea Primary Production.
  • Measurements view: four gridded fields (GLODAP, SOCAT, World Ocean Atlas and ocean oxygen) gain a third option beside the field and the hexagons, which draws the individual observations under each source's own quality rules.
  • Research cruise pages: a page for each of 9,201 GLODAP and SOCAT cruises with a track sketch and its sources.
  • 3D seamounts and hydrothermal vents: models on the map by default, with an Enhanced or Simple graphics switch.
  • OceanSITES history: moorings gain a historical record from the data centre's archive.
  • Area Export: can now include individual GLODAP casts, BGC-Argo oxygen profiles, SOCAT observations and WOD casts, with a stated cap.
  • N* in the World Ocean Atlas layer, labelled as derived, and a date or an explicit “none given” on every row of the nearest measurements.

Corrections are listed in the release notes and in the documentation record.

This record archives the software: a React + deck.gl frontend, a FastAPI + PostGIS backend, roughly 110 data-source synchronisation pipelines, an MVT tile server, baked raster field layers, an Area Export tool, a documented public read API, and the editorial and provenance logic that keeps the presentation neutral.

The platform's datasets are not included: a running deployment loads them from their upstream providers, each under its own licence. The only data in the repository are small verbatim excerpts used by the parser tests (about 5 MB in backend/tests/fixtures/), which stay under their upstream licences; see DATA-LICENCES.md. The per-source licence map, including non-commercial and mandatory-citation sources, is in DATA-LICENCES.md.

The methods, data sources, refresh strategies, derived products, known limitations and licensing model are documented separately in the companion deposit, doi:10.5281/zenodo.19745884 (CC-BY-4.0). This software record and that documentation record are two halves of one pair: cite the documentation for the method, this record for the code.
